title: API Gateway
subtitle: Centralized North-South edge proxy handling auth, rate limiting, TLS termination, and BFF aggregation.
keyTakeaways: An API Gateway is the single entry point for external (North-South) client traffic, decoupling clients from internal microservice topology.
Offloads cross-cutting concerns: TLS termination, JWT/OAuth validation, WAF, rate limiting, and protocol translation (REST/GraphQL to gRPC).
Keep business logic out of the API Gateway to prevent it from becoming a deployment bottleneck; use **Backends-for-Frontends (BFFs)** for client-specific aggregation.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: API Gateway is a foundational architectural concept in distributed systems. Centralized North-South edge proxy handling auth, rate limiting, TLS termination, and BFF aggregation. Fundamentally, Without an API Gateway, mobile and web clients would need to make dozens of direct requests to internal microservices over the public internet, exposing internal service topology, duplicating TLS and authentication logic across every service, and suffering high latency over slow cellular connections. An **API Gateway** (such as Envoy, Kong, AWS API Gateway, or APISIX) acts as the hardened reverse proxy at the perimeter of the system.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: An API Gateway is the single entry point for external (North-South) client traffic, decoupling clients from internal microservice topology.
**Problem Space & Invariants**: Offloads cross-cutting concerns: TLS termination, JWT/OAuth validation, WAF, rate limiting, and protocol translation (REST/GraphQL to gRPC).
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: In production distributed systems, api gateway manifests across several distinct architectural classifications, operational modes, and implementation strategies:
bullets: **Single Centralized API Gateway**: Focuses on single place to enforce security policies, rate limits, tls certificates, and observability. Best suited for Cross-cutting edge security, routing, and public developer APIs..

**Edge Gateway + Experience-Specific BFFs (Mobile BFF, Web BFF)**: Focuses on frontend teams own their own aggregation/graphql layer independently without touching edge security rules. Best suited for Multi-platform products serving Mobile, Web, TV, and Third-Party API consumers..

**Authentication & Identity Propagation**: Validates external OAuth2/OIDC tokens at the edge, then strips external headers and injects a trusted internal identity context (or mTLS SPIFFE ID) for downstream services.
**Rate Limiting & DDoS Protection**: Enforces per-IP, per-API-key, and per-tenant quotas before malicious traffic reaches internal compute.
**Header Spoofing Defense**: The API Gateway MUST strip any incoming `x-verified-user-id` headers sent by external clients before injecting its own verified identity headers.
**North-South vs East-West**: Internal service-to-service (East-West) calls should NEVER loop back out through the public North-South API Gateway.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Adopting appropriate design patterns around api gateway unlocks critical performance, scalability, and operational advantages for modern backend platforms:
bullets: **Where to Use — High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Cross-cutting edge security, routing, and public developer APIs. and environments requiring Single place to enforce security policies, rate limits, TLS certificates, and observability..

**Where to Use — High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Multi-platform products serving Mobile, Web, TV, and Third-Party API consumers. where Frontend teams own their own aggregation/GraphQL layer independently without touching edge security rules..

**How to Use — Engineering Implementation**: A common anti-pattern is stuffing complex domain orchestration, conditional branching, and payload transformations for iOS, Android, Web, and Smart TVs into a single centralized API Gateway owned by a platform team. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: While essential for scalable engineering, api gateway introduces substantial architectural trade-offs, operational failure modes, and anti-patterns if applied inappropriately:
bullets: **Where to Avoid — Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints impose can become an organizational bottleneck if product-specific aggregation logic is placed inside it.
**Where to Avoid — Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid premature optimization when requires maintaining additional lightweight bff deployments.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Mastering api gateway is a defining trait of Staff-level distributed systems engineers. Navigating the delicate balance between performance, reliability, and simplicity ensures architectures scale sustainably without introducing unmanageable operational friction.
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Keep business logic out of the API Gateway to prevent it from becoming a deployment bottleneck; use **Backends-for-Frontends (BFFs)** for client-specific aggregation.
**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Always mention **stripping internal identity headers (`x-user-id`) at the API Gateway** so malicious external users cannot spoof headers and impersonate other accounts.
